title: Introduce weighted init sequence and safe rollback annotations for private Helm charts
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Add configurable weighted init sequence to spread tenant init work across control plane windows.
- Introduce Helm annotations to mark resources as rollback-safe and preserve critical state (PVCs, ConfigMaps).
- Extend values.schema.json with initSequence.* fields and backoff/retry knobs for init jobs.
- No customer-facing API changes; installer behavior is opt-in and gated by values.initSequence.enabled.
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR adds a new, opt-in init sequencing mechanism to the Private Helm charts that lets operators spread tenant initialization work across a configurable number of weighted steps. The goal is to reduce large-scale init storms during installs/upgrades in multitenant/private installs and provide explicit Helm annotations that ensure safe rollbacks for stateful pieces during rollbacks.

What this changes (high level):
- New values under values.yaml: initSequence.enabled (bool), initSequence.steps (array of {name, weight, timeoutSeconds}), initSequence.concurrentLimit, initSequence.backoffPolicy, initSequence.maxRetries.
- A templated helper (_init.sequence.tpl) that renders Kubernetes Job/CronJob manifests according to weights and honors backoffLimit/restartPolicy values.
- Safe-rollback annotations added to the helm templates for PVC, secrets, and certain ConfigMaps: "rollback.redwood.com/safe": "true" and "rollback.redwood.com/preserve-on-rollback": "true"; chart tooling will skip destructive cleanup when those annotations are present.
- Updated Chart values.schema.json to validate the new keys and provide descriptive errors for misconfiguration.
- Documented a canary rollout pattern in charts/PRIVATE_INIT_README.md describing how to enable a gradual init with weights.

Compatibility and safety:
The feature is opt-in by default (values.initSequence.enabled: false) and deliberately additive. When disabled, chart behavior is unchanged. The rollback annotations are non-invasive strings attached to resources; they change Helm hooks/cleanup behavior only when the operator/installer uses the new rollback helper script.

Design notes and rationale:
Background: installs for some large customers were triggering mass tenant-checks and DB-migrate jobs concurrently which caused control-plane forwarding and temporary DB overload (linked SUP-1124). The weighted-init approach lets operators define e.g. 5 steps with weights [40, 30, 20, 5, 5] so most tenants go through early steps but heavy work is throttled into later windows.
Implementation details:
- Template uses named template partials to keep per-resource logic simple and testable. initSequence.steps is iterated and rendered as Job manifests that select tenants by label/annotation (installer-provided selector). Jobs include an owner-reference optional flag so that tenants can be reconciled independently.
- Backoff/retry knobs map to Job.backoffLimit and activeDeadlineSeconds. For legacy clusters that do not support Jobs with certain fields the chart falls back to a CronJob-based shim.
- A new lua/helm helper script in scripts/rollback-safety.sh is included to detect "rollback.redwood.com/safe" annotations during helm rollback and skip destructive deletes for resources with that annotation. This script is small and only used when the operator chooses rollback-safe mode.

Testing performed:
- Unit: values.schema.json validation tests for common misconfigurations.
- Integration: kind-based e2e that simulates 200 tenant resources and runs initSequence with different weight distributions; verified CPU/memory profiles during init windows and observed reduced peak concurrency compared to baseline.
- Upgrade test: dry-run helm upgrade with initSequence enabled/disabled; verified no template regressions.
- Manual QA: ran the new rollback helper against a staging cluster and confirmed PVCs annotated with preserve-on-rollback are left intact on helm rollback (SUP-1124 reproduction case).

Rollout plan and migration guidance:
1) Merge to main and cut a patch chart release.
2) Operators should enable values.initSequence.enabled=false and validate in staging.
3) For customers with large tenant counts, recommend staged enablement: enable initSequence and start with a 10-step distribution with low concurrency, monitor control-plane metrics, then tune weights.
4) To use rollback-safety, operators must enable the scripts in their installer flow; default behavior remains the same.

Checklist:
- [x] values.schema.json updated with descriptions and examples
- [x] Helm templates added in templates/_init.sequence.tpl and referenced from templates/init-jobs.yaml
- [x] rollback helper script included in scripts/rollback-safety.sh
- [x] Integration tests added to .github/workflows/helm-e2e.yml
- [x] Docs added to charts/PRIVATE_INIT_README.md with example weight matrices

Related: ENG-3421 (init sequencing design), ENG-3499 (rollback safety), SUP-1124 (customer incident).

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on values.schema.json correctness and the template conditional paths for clusters that do not support CronJob TTLs.
- I intentionally split the job vs cronjob path into two small templates to make unit tests easier.

- Design doc (internal): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/init-sequence-design
- Incident: https://support.redwood.com/cases/SUP-1124
